note: next_jsonapi is a pure service-decoration module: NextJsonapiServiceProvider::alter() re-classes jsonapi.entity_resource to Drupal\next_jsonapi\Controller\EntityResource and calls setMaxSize('%next_jsonapi.size_max%'), with parameter next_jsonapi.size_max = 1000 (core JSON:API max is 50). It has no config entity/permission/route/Drush, so its only live 'state' is the active service class + the container parameter, and whether the module is enabled. Introspection reads get_class(jsonapi.entity_resource) and the size_max parameter from the running container; execution is grounded in enabling/uninstalling the module, verified by whether jsonapi.entity_resource is next_jsonapi's subclass. Actual JSON:API traffic is consumed by the external Next.js app.

evals.prompt: What does the next_jsonapi submodule do for a decoupled Next.js site?
evals.expected_output: It raises JSON:API's maximum page size to 1000 (core default is 50) by decorating the jsonapi.entity_resource service with its own EntityResource subclass, so a Next.js build can fetch large collections in fewer requests.

evals.prompt: Which container parameter controls the maximum JSON:API page size in next_jsonapi, and what is its default value?
evals.expected_output: The parameter next_jsonapi.size_max, defined in next_jsonapi.services.yml with default value 1000. Override it (e.g. in a services.yml) to change the cap; there is no admin form.

evals.prompt: How does next_jsonapi apply its higher page-size limit technically?
evals.expected_output: NextJsonapiServiceProvider::alter() changes the jsonapi.entity_resource service class to Drupal\next_jsonapi\Controller\EntityResource and adds a setMaxSize('%next_jsonapi.size_max%') method call. That subclass overrides getJsonApiParams() to use the larger OffsetPage max when a 'fields' query parameter is present.

evals.prompt: On this live site, inspect the service container and report which PHP class currently serves the jsonapi.entity_resource service (indicating next_jsonapi's decoration is active).
evals.expected_output: get_class(\Drupal::service('jsonapi.entity_resource')) is Drupal\next_jsonapi\Controller\EntityResource, showing next_jsonapi has decorated the core service.

evals.prompt: Inspect the running Drupal container on this site and report the value of the next_jsonapi.size_max parameter (the JSON:API max page size next_jsonapi sets).
I need my headless Next.js site to be able to pull large JSON:API collections (bigger pages) from Drupal. Enable the next_jsonapi module so JSON:API's page-size limit is raised for the front end.
evals.expected_output: next_jsonapi is enabled, so the jsonapi.entity_resource service is now Drupal\next_jsonapi\Controller\EntityResource and the next_jsonapi.size_max parameter (1000) is defined.

evals.prompt: We are moving this decoupled site from JSON:API to another data layer and no longer want next_jsonapi's JSON:API page-size override. Uninstall the next_jsonapi module (leave the core jsonapi and next modules in place).
evals.expected_output: next_jsonapi is no longer enabled; jsonapi.entity_resource has reverted to the core Drupal\jsonapi\Controller\EntityResource class (not next_jsonapi's subclass), while jsonapi and next remain enabled.
